occupations.description: Set up or operate a variety of drills to remove underground oil and gas, or remove core samples for testing during oil and gas exploration.
titles: Oil Operations Management Professional (Oil Ops Management Professional)
Gas Operations Management Professional (Gas Ops Management Professional)

occupations.title: Service Unit Operators, Oil and Gas
occupations.description: Operate equipment to increase oil flow from producing wells or to remove stuck pipe, casing, tools, or other obstructions from drilling wells. Includes fishing-tool technicians.
titles: Oil and Shale and Tar Processing Technician

occupations.title: Excavating and Loading Machine and Dragline Operators, Surface Mining
occupations.description: Operate or tend machinery at surface mining site, equipped with scoops, shovels, or buckets to excavate and load loose materials.

occupations.title: Earth Drillers, Except Oil and Gas
occupations.description: Operate a variety of drills such as rotary, churn, and pneumatic to tap subsurface water and salt deposits, to remove core samples during mineral exploration or soil testing, and to facilitate the use of explosives in mining or construction. Includes horizontal and earth boring machine operators.

occupations.title: Explosives Workers, Ordnance Handling Experts, and Blasters
occupations.description: Place and detonate explosives to demolish structures or to loosen, remove, or displace earth, rock, or other materials. May perform specialized handling, storage, and accounting procedures.

occupations.title: Continuous Mining Machine Operators
occupations.description: Operate self-propelled mining machines that rip coal, metal and nonmetal ores, rock, stone, or sand from the mine face and load it onto conveyors, shuttle cars, or trucks in a continuous operation.

occupations.title: Roof Bolters, Mining
occupations.description: Operate machinery to install roof support bolts in underground mine.

occupations.title: Loading and Moving Machine Operators, Underground Mining
occupations.description: Operate underground loading or moving machine to load or move coal, ore, or rock using shuttle or mine car or conveyors. Equipment may include power shovels, hoisting engines equipped with cable-drawn scraper or scoop, or machines equipped with gathering arms and conveyor.

occupations.title: Rock Splitters, Quarry
occupations.description: Separate blocks of rough dimension stone from quarry mass using jackhammers, wedges, or chop saws.

occupations.title: Roustabouts, Oil and Gas
occupations.description: Assemble or repair oil field equipment using hand and power tools. Perform other tasks as needed.
titles: Generator Field Service Technician (Generator Field Service Tech)
Field Service Installation Technician (Field Service Installation Tech)

occupations.title: Helpers--Extraction Workers
occupations.description: Help extraction craft workers, such as earth drillers, blasters and explosives workers, derrick operators, and mining machine operators, by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include supplying equipment or cleaning work area.

occupations.title: First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
occupations.description: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of mechanics, installers, and repairers. May also advise customers on recommended services. Excludes team or work leaders.

occupations.title: Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers
occupations.description: Repair, maintain, or install computers, word processing systems, automated teller machines, and electronic office machines, such as duplicating and fax machines.

occupations.title: Radio, Cellular, and Tower Equipment Installers and Repairers
occupations.description: Repair, install, or maintain mobile or stationary radio transmitting, broadcasting, and receiving equipment, and two-way radio communications systems used in cellular telecommunications, mobile broadband, ship-to-shore, aircraft-to-ground communications, and radio equipment in service and emergency vehicles. May test and analyze network coverage.

occupations.title: Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers, Except Line Installers
occupations.description: Install, set up, rearrange, or remove switching, distribution, routing, and dialing equipment used in central offices or headends. Service or repair telephone, cable television, Internet, and other communications equipment on customers' property. May install communications equipment or communications wiring in buildings.

occupations.title: Avionics Technicians
occupations.description: Install, inspect, test, adjust, or repair avionics equipment, such as radar, radio, navigation, and missile control systems in aircraft or space vehicles.

occupations.title: Electric Motor, Power Tool, and Related Repairers
occupations.description: Repair, maintain, or install electric motors, wiring, or switches.

occupations.title: Electrical and Electronics Installers and Repairers, Transportation Equipment
occupations.description: Install, adjust, or maintain mobile electronics communication equipment, including sound, sonar, security, navigation, and surveillance systems on trains, watercraft, or other mobile equipment.

occupations.title: Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Commercial and Industrial Equipment
occupations.description: Repair, test, adjust, or install electronic equipment, such as industrial controls, transmitters, and antennas.

occupations.title: Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Powerhouse, Substation, and Relay
occupations.description: Inspect, test, repair, or maintain electrical equipment in generating stations, substations, and in-service relays.
titles: On Site Service Tech (On Site Service Technician)
Instrument and Control Technician (I and C Technician)
Instrumentation and Control Technician (I and C Technician)

occupations.title: Electronic Equipment Installers and Repairers, Motor Vehicles
occupations.description: Install, diagnose, or repair communications, sound, security, or navigation equipment in motor vehicles.
titles: GPS Navigation Installer (Global Positioning System Navigation Installer)
GPS Car Navigation Installer (Global Positioning System Car Navigation Installer)

occupations.title: Audiovisual Equipment Installers and Repairers
occupations.description: Install, repair, or adjust audio or television receivers, stereo systems, camcorders, video systems, or other electronic entertainment equipment in homes or other venues. May perform routine maintenance.

occupations.title: Security and Fire Alarm Systems Installers
occupations.description: Install, program, maintain, and repair security and fire alarm wiring and equipment. Ensure that work is in accordance with relevant codes.
titles: Fire Alarm Inspection Test Maintenance Technician
Special Hazards Fire Suppression System Technician

occupations.title: Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians
occupations.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul aircraft engines and assemblies, such as hydraulic and pneumatic systems.

occupations.title: Automotive Body and Related Repairers
occupations.description: Repair and refinish automotive vehicle bodies and straighten vehicle frames.

occupations.title: Automotive Glass Installers and Repairers
occupations.description: Replace or repair broken windshields and window glass in motor vehicles.
titles: Auto Glass Repair Specialist (Automotive Glass Repair Specialist)
Auto Services Glass Installer (Automotive Services Glass Installer)

occupations.title: Automotive Service Technicians and Mechanics
occupations.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul automotive vehicles.

occupations.title: Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists
occupations.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul buses and trucks, or maintain and repair any type of diesel engines. Includes mechanics working primarily with automobile or marine diesel engines.

occupations.title: Farm Equipment Mechanics and Service Technicians
occupations.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul farm machinery and vehicles, such as tractors, harvesters, dairy equipment, and irrigation systems.

occupations.title: Mobile Heavy Equipment Mechanics, Except Engines
occupations.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul mobile mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic equipment, such as cranes, bulldozers, graders, and conveyors, used in construction, logging, and mining.

occupations.title: Rail Car Repairers
occupations.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul railroad rolling stock, mine cars, or mass transit rail cars.

occupations.title: Motorboat Mechanics and Service Technicians
occupations.description: Repair and adjust electrical and mechanical equipment of inboard or inboard-outboard boat engines.

occupations.title: Motorcycle Mechanics
occupations.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul motorcycles, scooters, mopeds, dirt bikes, or similar motorized vehicles.

occupations.title: Outdoor Power Equipment and Other Small Engine Mechanics
occupations.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul small engines used to power lawn mowers, chain saws, recreational sporting equipment, and related equipment.

occupations.title: Bicycle Repairers
occupations.description: Repair and service bicycles.

occupations.title: Recreational Vehicle Service Technicians
occupations.description: Diagnose, inspect, adjust, repair, or overhaul recreational vehicles including travel trailers. May specialize in maintaining gas, electrical, hydraulic, plumbing, or chassis/towing systems as well as repairing generators, appliances, and interior components. Includes workers who perform customized van conversions.
titles: RV Body Mechanic (Recreational Vehicle Body Mechanic)
RV Repair Technician (Recreational Vehicle Repair Technician)
RV Service Technician (Recreational Vehicle Service Technician)
Certified RV Technician (Certified Recreational Vehicle Technician)
Mobile Service RV Technician (Mobile Service Recreational Vehicle Technician)
RVDA Master Certified RV Technician (Recreational Vehicle Dealer Association Master Certified Recreational Vehicle Technician)

occupations.title: Tire Repairers and Changers
occupations.description: Repair and replace tires.
titles: Commercial Tire Service Technician (Commercial Tire Service Tech)

occupations.title: Mechanical Door Repairers
occupations.description: Install, service, or repair automatic door mechanisms and hydraulic doors. Includes garage door mechanics.
titles: Garage Door Service Technician (Garage Door Service Tech)

occupations.title: Control and Valve Installers and Repairers, Except Mechanical Door
occupations.description: Install, repair, and maintain mechanical regulating and controlling devices, such as electric meters, gas regulators, thermostats, safety and flow valves, and other mechanical governors.

occupations.title: Heating, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration Mechanics and Installers
occupations.description: Install or repair heating, central air conditioning, HVAC, or refrigeration systems, including oil burners, hot-air furnaces, and heating stoves.
titles: AC Service Tech (Air Conditioning Service Technician)
Heating and AC Tech (Heating and Air Conditioning Technician)
Heating and AC Servicer (Heating and Air Conditioning Servicer)
HVAC Tech (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning Technician)
Heating and AC Installer (Heating and Air Conditioning Installer)
HVAC Mechanic (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning Mechanic)
HVAC Installer (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning Installer)
HVACR Tech (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning Refrigeration Technician)
HVACR Tech (Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration Technician)

occupations.title: Home Appliance Repairers
occupations.description: Repair, adjust, or install all types of electric or gas household appliances, such as refrigerators, washers, dryers, and ovens.

occupations.title: Industrial Machinery Mechanics
occupations.description: Repair, install, adjust, or maintain industrial production and processing machinery or refinery and pipeline distribution systems. May also install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to plans.

occupations.title: Maintenance Workers, Machinery
occupations.description: Lubricate machinery, change parts, or perform other routine machinery maintenance.

occupations.title: Millwrights
occupations.description: Install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to layout plans, blueprints, or other drawings.
titles: Machine Set Up Operator (Machine Set Up Op)
Automobile Equipment Technician Engineer (Auto Equipment Tech Engineer)
Automobile Equipment Engineer Technician (Auto Equipment Engineer Tech)
Automated Equipment Engineering Technician (Automated Equipment Engineering Tech)

occupations.title: Refractory Materials Repairers, Except Brickmasons
occupations.description: Build or repair equipment such as furnaces, kilns, cupolas, boilers, converters, ladles, soaking pits, and ovens, using refractory materials.

occupations.title: Electrical Power-Line Installers and Repairers
occupations.description: Install or repair cables or wires used in electrical power or distribution systems. May erect poles and light or heavy duty transmission towers.

occupations.title: Telecommunications Line Installers and Repairers
occupations.description: Install and repair telecommunications cable, including fiber optics.

occupations.title: Camera and Photographic Equipment Repairers
occupations.description: Repair and adjust cameras and photographic equipment, including commercial video and motion picture camera equipment.

occupations.title: Medical Equipment Repairers
occupations.description: Test, adjust, or repair biomedical or electromedical equipment.
titles: Medical Equipment Service Tech (Medical Equipment Service Technician)
Biomedical Equipment Support Specialist (Biomed Equipment Support Specialist)

occupations.title: Musical Instrument Repairers and Tuners
occupations.description: Repair percussion, stringed, reed, or wind instruments. May specialize in one area, such as piano tuning.

occupations.title: Watch and Clock Repairers
occupations.description: Repair, clean, and adjust mechanisms of timing instruments, such as watches and clocks. Includes watchmakers, watch technicians, and mechanical timepiece repairers.

occupations.title: Maintenance and Repair Workers, General
occupations.description: Perform work involving the skills of two or more maintenance or craft occupations to keep machines, mechanical equipment, or the structure of a building in repair. Duties may involve pipe fitting; HVAC maintenance; insulating; welding; machining; carpentry; repairing electrical or mechanical equipment; installing, aligning, and balancing new equipment; and repairing buildings, floors, or stairs.

occupations.title: Wind Turbine Service Technicians
occupations.description: Inspect, diagnose, adjust, or repair wind turbines. Perform maintenance on wind turbine equipment including resolving electrical, mechanical, and hydraulic malfunctions.
titles: Wind Turbine Blade Composite Technician (Wind Turbine Blade Composite Tech)

occupations.title: Coin, Vending, and Amusement Machine Servicers and Repairers
occupations.description: Install, service, adjust, or repair coin, vending, or amusement machines including video games, juke boxes, pinball machines, or slot machines.

occupations.title: Commercial Divers
occupations.description: Work below surface of water, using surface-supplied air or scuba equipment to inspect, repair, remove, or install equipment and structures. May use a variety of power and hand tools, such as drills, sledgehammers, torches, and welding equipment. May conduct tests or experiments, rig explosives, or photograph structures or marine life.
titles: NDT UW Welder (Non Destructive Testing Under Water Welder)

occupations.title: Locksmiths and Safe Repairers
occupations.description: Repair and open locks, make keys, change locks and safe combinations, and install and repair safes.

occupations.title: Manufactured Building and Mobile Home Installers
occupations.description: Move or install mobile homes or prefabricated buildings.

occupations.title: Riggers
occupations.description: Set up or repair rigging for construction projects, manufacturing plants, logging yards, ships and shipyards, or for the entertainment industry.

occupations.title: Signal and Track Switch Repairers
occupations.description: Install, inspect, test, maintain, or repair electric gate crossings, signals, signal equipment, track switches, section lines, or intercommunications systems within a railroad system.

occupations.title: Helpers--Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers
occupations.description: Help installation, maintenance, and repair workers in maintenance, parts replacement, and repair of vehicles, industrial machinery, and electrical and electronic equipment. Perform duties such as furnishing tools, materials, and supplies to other workers; cleaning work area, machines, and tools; and holding materials or tools for other workers.

occupations.title: Geothermal Technicians
occupations.description: Perform technical activities at power plants or individual installations necessary for the generation of power from geothermal energy sources. Monitor and control operating activities at geothermal power generation facilities and perform maintenance and repairs as necessary. Install, test, and maintain residential and commercial geothermal heat pumps.
titles: Ground Source Heat Pump Technician (GSHP Technician)
I and C Technician (Instrument and Controls Technician)
Operations and Maintenance Technician (O and M Technician)
I and E Technician (Instrumentation and Electrical Technician)
I C and E Technician (Instrumentation, Control, and Electrical Technician)
Geothermal HVAC Technician (Geothermal Heating, Ventilating, and Air Conditioning Technician)

occupations.title: First-Line Supervisors of Production and Operating Workers
occupations.description: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of production and operating workers, such as inspectors, precision workers, machine setters and operators, assemblers, fabricators, and plant and system operators. Excludes team or work leaders.

occupations.title: Aircraft Structure, Surfaces, Rigging, and Systems Assemblers
occupations.description: Assemble, fit, fasten, and install parts of airplanes, space vehicles, or missiles, such as tails, wings, fuselage, bulkheads, stabilizers, landing gear, rigging and control equipment, or heating and ventilating systems.

occupations.title: Coil Winders, Tapers, and Finishers
occupations.description: Wind wire coils used in electrical components, such as resistors and transformers, and in electrical equipment and instruments, such as field cores, bobbins, armature cores, electrical motors, generators, and control equipment.

occupations.title: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Assemblers
occupations.description: Assemble or modify electrical or electronic equipment, such as computers, test equipment telemetering systems, electric motors, and batteries.

occupations.title: Electromechanical Equipment Assemblers
occupations.description: Assemble or modify electromechanical equipment or devices, such as servomechanisms, gyros, dynamometers, magnetic drums, tape drives, brakes, control linkage, actuators, and appliances.

occupations.title: Engine and Other Machine Assemblers
occupations.description: Construct, assemble, or rebuild machines, such as engines, turbines, and similar equipment used in such industries as construction, extraction, textiles, and paper manufacturing.

occupations.title: Structural Metal Fabricators and Fitters
occupations.description: Fabricate, position, align, and fit parts of structural metal products.

occupations.title: Fiberglass Laminators and Fabricators
occupations.description: Laminate layers of fiberglass on molds to form boat decks and hulls, bodies for golf carts, automobiles, or other products.

occupations.title: Timing Device Assemblers and Adjusters
occupations.description: Perform precision assembling or adjusting, within narrow tolerances, of timing devices such as digital clocks or timing devices with electrical or electronic components.

occupations.title: Team Assemblers
occupations.description: Work as part of a team having responsibility for assembling an entire product or component of a product. Team assemblers can perform all tasks conducted by the team in the assembly process and rotate through all or most of them, rather than being assigned to a specific task on a permanent basis. May participate in making management decisions affecting the work. Includes team leaders who work as part of the team.
titles: Delivery and Assembly Technician (Delivery and Assembly Tech)

occupations.title: Bakers
occupations.description: Mix and bake ingredients to produce breads, rolls, cookies, cakes, pies, pastries, or other baked goods.

occupations.title: Butchers and Meat Cutters
occupations.description: Cut, trim, or prepare consumer-sized portions of meat for use or sale in retail establishments.

occupations.title: Meat, Poultry, and Fish Cutters and Trimmers
occupations.description: Use hands or hand tools to perform routine cutting and trimming of meat, poultry, and seafood.

occupations.title: Slaughterers and Meat Packers
occupations.description: Perform nonroutine or precision functions involving the preparation of large portions of meat. Work may include specialized slaughtering tasks, cutting standard or premium cuts of meat for marketing, making sausage, or wrapping meats. Work typically occurs in slaughtering, meat packing, or wholesale establishments.

occupations.title: Food and Tobacco Roasting, Baking, and Drying Machine Operators and Tenders
occupations.description: Operate or tend food or tobacco roasting, baking, or drying equipment, including hearth ovens, kiln driers, roasters, char kilns, and vacuum drying equipment.

occupations.title: Food Batchmakers
occupations.description: Set up and operate equipment that mixes or blends ingredients used in the manufacturing of food products. Includes candy makers and cheese makers.

occupations.title: Food Cooking Machine Operators and Tenders
occupations.description: Operate or tend cooking equipment, such as steam cooking vats, deep fry cookers, pressure cookers, kettles, and boilers, to prepare food products.

occupations.title: Extruding and Drawing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to extrude or draw thermoplastic or metal materials into tubes, rods, hoses, wire, bars, or structural shapes.

occupations.title: Forging Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend forging machines to taper, shape, or form metal or plastic parts.

occupations.title: Rolling Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to roll steel or plastic forming bends, beads, knurls, rolls, or plate, or to flatten, temper, or reduce gauge of material.

occupations.title: Cutting, Punching, and Press Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to saw, cut, shear, slit, punch, crimp, notch, bend, or straighten metal or plastic material.

occupations.title: Drilling and Boring Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend drilling machines to drill, bore, ream, mill, or countersink metal or plastic work pieces.

occupations.title: Grinding, Lapping, Polishing, and Buffing Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend grinding and related tools that remove excess material or burrs from surfaces, sharpen edges or corners, or buff, hone, or polish metal or plastic work pieces.

occupations.title: Lathe and Turning Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend lathe and turning machines to turn, bore, thread, form, or face metal or plastic materials, such as wire, rod, or bar stock.

occupations.title: Milling and Planing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend milling or planing machines to mill, plane, shape, groove, or profile metal or plastic work pieces.

occupations.title: Machinists
occupations.description: Set up and operate a variety of machine tools to produce precision parts and instruments out of metal. Includes precision instrument makers who fabricate, modify, or repair mechanical instruments. May also fabricate and modify parts to make or repair machine tools or maintain industrial machines, applying knowledge of mechanics, mathematics, metal properties, layout, and machining procedures.

occupations.title: Metal-Refining Furnace Operators and Tenders
occupations.description: Operate or tend furnaces, such as gas, oil, coal, electric-arc or electric induction, open-hearth, or oxygen furnaces, to melt and refine metal before casting or to produce specified types of steel.

occupations.title: Pourers and Casters, Metal
occupations.description: Operate hand-controlled mechanisms to pour and regulate the flow of molten metal into molds to produce castings or ingots.

occupations.title: Model Makers, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Set up and operate machines, such as lathes, milling and engraving machines, and jig borers to make working models of metal or plastic objects. Includes template makers.

occupations.title: Patternmakers, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Lay out, machine, fit, and assemble castings and parts to metal or plastic foundry patterns, core boxes, or match plates.

occupations.title: Foundry Mold and Coremakers
occupations.description: Make or form wax or sand cores or molds used in the production of metal castings in foundries.

occupations.title: Molding, Coremaking, and Casting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend metal or plastic molding, casting, or coremaking machines to mold or cast metal or thermoplastic parts or products.

occupations.title: Multiple Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend more than one type of cutting or forming machine tool or robot.

occupations.title: Tool and Die Makers
occupations.description: Analyze specifications, lay out metal stock, set up and operate machine tools, and fit and assemble parts to make and repair dies, cutting tools, jigs, fixtures, gauges, and machinists' hand tools.

occupations.title: Welders, Cutters, Solderers, and Brazers
occupations.description: Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products.

occupations.title: Welding, Soldering, and Brazing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend welding, soldering, or brazing machines or robots that weld, braze, solder, or heat treat metal products, components, or assemblies. Includes workers who operate laser cutters or laser-beam machines.

occupations.title: Heat Treating Equipment Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend heating equipment, such as heat-treating furnaces, flame-hardening machines, induction machines, soaking pits, or vacuum equipment to temper, harden, anneal, or heat treat metal or plastic objects.

occupations.title: Layout Workers, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Lay out reference points and dimensions on metal or plastic stock or workpieces, such as sheets, plates, tubes, structural shapes, castings, or machine parts, for further processing. Includes shipfitters.

occupations.title: Plating Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend plating machines to coat metal or plastic products with chromium, zinc, copper, cadmium, nickel, or other metal to protect or decorate surfaces. Typically, the product being coated is immersed in molten metal or an electrolytic solution.

occupations.title: Tool Grinders, Filers, and Sharpeners
occupations.description: Perform precision smoothing, sharpening, polishing, or grinding of metal objects.
titles: OD Grinder Operator (Outer Diameter Grinder Operator)
Cutter Grind Tool Technician (Cutter Grind Tool Tech)

occupations.title: Prepress Technicians and Workers
occupations.description: Format and proof text and images submitted by designers and clients into finished pages that can be printed. Includes digital and photo typesetting. May produce printing plates.

occupations.title: Printing Press Operators
occupations.description: Set up and operate digital, letterpress, lithographic, flexographic, gravure, or other printing machines. Includes short-run offset printing presses.

occupations.title: Print Binding and Finishing Workers
occupations.description: Bind books and other publications or finish printed products by hand or machine. May set up binding and finishing machines.

occupations.title: Laundry and Dry-Cleaning Workers
occupations.description: Operate or tend washing or dry-cleaning machines to wash or dry-clean industrial or household articles, such as cloth garments, suede, leather, furs, blankets, draperies, linens, rugs, and carpets. Includes spotters and dyers of these articles.

occupations.title: Pressers, Textile, Garment, and Related Materials
occupations.description: Press or shape articles by hand or machine.

occupations.title: Sewing Machine Operators
occupations.description: Operate or tend sewing machines to join, reinforce, decorate, or perform related sewing operations in the manufacture of garment or nongarment products.

occupations.title: Shoe and Leather Workers and Repairers
occupations.description: Construct, decorate, or repair leather and leather-like products, such as luggage, shoes, and saddles. May use hand tools.

occupations.title: Shoe Machine Operators and Tenders
occupations.description: Operate or tend a variety of machines to join, decorate, reinforce, or finish shoes and shoe parts.

occupations.title: Sewers, Hand
occupations.description: Sew, join, reinforce, or finish, usually with needle and thread, a variety of manufactured items. Includes weavers and stitchers.

occupations.title: Tailors, Dressmakers, and Custom Sewers
occupations.description: Design, make, alter, repair, or fit garments.

occupations.title: Textile Bleaching and Dyeing Machine Operators and Tenders
occupations.description: Operate or tend machines to bleach, shrink, wash, dye, or finish textiles or synthetic or glass fibers.

occupations.title: Textile Cutting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that cut textiles.

occupations.title: Textile Knitting and Weaving Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that knit, loop, weave, or draw in textiles.

occupations.title: Textile Winding, Twisting, and Drawing Out Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that wind or twist textiles; or draw out and combine sliver, such as wool, hemp, or synthetic fibers. Includes slubber machine and drawing frame operators.

occupations.title: Extruding and Forming Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Synthetic and Glass Fibers
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that extrude and form continuous filaments from synthetic materials, such as liquid polymer, rayon, and fiberglass.

occupations.title: Fabric and Apparel Patternmakers
occupations.description: Draw and construct sets of precision master fabric patterns or layouts. May also mark and cut fabrics and apparel.

occupations.title: Upholsterers
occupations.description: Make, repair, or replace upholstery for household furniture or transportation vehicles.

occupations.title: Cabinetmakers and Bench Carpenters
occupations.description: Cut, shape, and assemble wooden articles or set up and operate a variety of woodworking machines, such as power saws, jointers, and mortisers to surface, cut, or shape lumber or to fabricate parts for wood products.

occupations.title: Furniture Finishers
occupations.description: Shape, finish, and refinish damaged, worn, or used furniture or new high-grade furniture to specified color or finish.

occupations.title: Model Makers, Wood
occupations.description: Construct full-size and scale wooden precision models of products. Includes wood jig builders and loft workers.

occupations.title: Patternmakers, Wood
occupations.description: Plan, lay out, and construct wooden unit or sectional patterns used in forming sand molds for castings.

occupations.title: Sawing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Wood
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend wood sawing machines. May operate computer numerically controlled (CNC) equipment. Includes lead sawyers.

occupations.title: Woodworking Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Except Sawing
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend woodworking machines, such as drill presses, lathes, shapers, routers, sanders, planers, and wood nailing machines. May operate computer numerically controlled (CNC) equipment.

occupations.title: Nuclear Power Reactor Operators
occupations.description: Operate or control nuclear reactors. Move control rods, start and stop equipment, monitor and adjust controls, and record data in logs. Implement emergency procedures when needed. May respond to abnormalities, determine cause, and recommend corrective action.
titles: Nuclear Power Plant Process Control Worker

occupations.title: Power Distributors and Dispatchers
occupations.description: Coordinate, regulate, or distribute electricity or steam.
titles: Electrical Energy Storage Technician (Electrical Energy Storage Tech)
Switchboard and Control Room Operator (SWB and Control Room Operator)
Electrical Energy Distribution Technician (Electrical Energy Distribution Tech)

occupations.title: Power Plant Operators
occupations.description: Control, operate, or maintain machinery to generate electric power. Includes auxiliary equipment operators.

occupations.title: Biomass Plant Technicians
occupations.description: Control and monitor biomass plant activities and perform maintenance as needed.

occupations.title: Hydroelectric Plant Technicians
occupations.description: Monitor and control activities associated with hydropower generation. Operate plant equipment, such as turbines, pumps, valves, gates, fans, electric control boards, and battery banks. Monitor equipment operation and performance and make necessary adjustments to ensure optimal performance. Perform equipment maintenance and repair as necessary.
titles: Operations and Maintenance Technician (O and M Technician)
Communications and Instrumentation Mechanic (C and I Mechanic)
Hydroelectric Operations and Maintenance Technician (Hydro O and M Technician)
Hydroelectric Plant Installation Technician (Hydroelectric Plant Installation Tech)
Hydroelectric Operations Maintenance Technician (Hydroelectric Operations Maintenance Tech)
Hydroelectric Plant Operations and Maintenance Technician (Hydroelectric Plant O and M Tech)

occupations.title: Stationary Engineers and Boiler Operators
occupations.description: Operate or maintain stationary engines, boilers, or other mechanical equipment to provide utilities for buildings or industrial processes. Operate equipment such as steam engines, generators, motors, turbines, and steam boilers.

occupations.title: Water and Wastewater Treatment Plant and System Operators
occupations.description: Operate or control an entire process or system of machines, often through the use of control boards, to transfer or treat water or wastewater.

occupations.title: Chemical Plant and System Operators
occupations.description: Control or operate entire chemical processes or system of machines.
titles: Chemical Treatment Plant Technician (Chemical Treatment Plant Tech)
Chemical Plant Operations Technician (Chemical Plan Operations Tech)

occupations.title: Gas Plant Operators
occupations.description: Distribute or process gas for utility companies and others by controlling compressors to maintain specified pressures on main pipelines.

occupations.title: Petroleum Pump System Operators, Refinery Operators, and Gaugers
occupations.description: Operate or control petroleum refining or processing units. May specialize in controlling manifold and pumping systems, gauging or testing oil in storage tanks, or regulating the flow of oil into pipelines.

occupations.title: Biofuels Processing Technicians
occupations.description: Calculate, measure, load, mix, and process refined feedstock with additives in fermentation or reaction process vessels and monitor production process. Perform, and keep records of, plant maintenance, repairs, and safety inspections.

occupations.title: Chemical Equipment Operators and Tenders
occupations.description: Operate or tend equipment to control chemical changes or reactions in the processing of industrial or consumer products. Equipment used includes devulcanizers, steam-jacketed kettles, and reactor vessels.

occupations.title: Separating, Filtering, Clarifying, Precipitating, and Still Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend continuous flow or vat-type equipment; filter presses; shaker screens; centrifuges; condenser tubes; precipitating, fermenting, or evaporating tanks; scrubbing towers; or batch stills. These machines extract, sort, or separate liquids, gases, or solids from other materials to recover a refined product. Includes dairy processing equipment operators.

occupations.title: Crushing, Grinding, and Polishing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to crush, grind, or polish materials, such as coal, glass, grain, stone, food, or rubber.

occupations.title: Grinding and Polishing Workers, Hand
occupations.description: Grind, sand, or polish, using hand tools or hand-held power tools, a variety of metal, wood, stone, clay, plastic, or glass objects. Includes chippers, buffers, and finishers.

occupations.title: Mixing and Blending Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to mix or blend materials, such as chemicals, tobacco, liquids, color pigments, or explosive ingredients.

occupations.title: Cutters and Trimmers, Hand
occupations.description: Use hand tools or hand-held power tools to cut and trim a variety of manufactured items, such as carpet, fabric, stone, glass, or rubber.

occupations.title: Cutting and Slicing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that cut or slice materials, such as glass, stone, cork, rubber, tobacco, food, paper, or insulating material.

occupations.title: Extruding, Forming, Pressing, and Compacting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines, such as glass-forming machines, plodder machines, and tuber machines, to shape and form products such as glassware, food, rubber, soap, brick, tile, clay, wax, tobacco, or cosmetics.

occupations.title: Furnace, Kiln, Oven, Drier, and Kettle Operators and Tenders
occupations.description: Operate or tend heating equipment other than basic metal, plastic, or food processing equipment. Includes activities such as annealing glass, drying lumber, curing rubber, removing moisture from materials, or boiling soap.

occupations.title: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
occupations.description: Inspect, test, sort, sample, or weigh nonagricultural raw materials or processed, machined, fabricated, or assembled parts or products for defects, wear, and deviations from specifications. May use precision measuring instruments and complex test equipment.

occupations.title: Jewelers and Precious Stone and Metal Workers
occupations.description: Design, fabricate, adjust, repair, or appraise jewelry, gold, silver, other precious metals, or gems.

occupations.title: Gem and Diamond Workers
occupations.description: Fabricate, finish, or evaluate the quality of gems and diamonds used in jewelry or industrial tools.

occupations.title: Dental Laboratory Technicians
occupations.description: Construct and repair full or partial dentures or dental appliances.
titles: Crown and Bridge Technician (Crown and Bridge Tech)
Metal Room Dental Technician (Metal Room Dental Tech)
Orthotic and Prosthetic Technician (Orthotic and Prosthetic Tech)

occupations.title: Medical Appliance Technicians
occupations.description: Construct, maintain, or repair medical supportive devices such as braces, orthotics and prosthetic devices, joints, arch supports, and other surgical and medical appliances.
titles: Hearing Aid Repair Technician (Hearing Aid Repair Tech)
Orthotic Finish Grinding Technician (Orthotic Finish Grinding Tech)
Registered Prosthetic Orthotic Technician (Registered Prosthetic Orthotic Tech)

occupations.title: Ophthalmic Laboratory Technicians
occupations.description: Cut, grind, and polish eyeglasses, contact lenses, or other precision optical elements. Assemble and mount lenses into frames or process other optical elements. Includes precision lens polishers or grinders, centerer-edgers, and lens mounters.

occupations.title: Packaging and Filling Machine Operators and Tenders
occupations.description: Operate or tend machines to prepare industrial or consumer products for storage or shipment. Includes cannery workers who pack food products.

occupations.title: Painting, Coating, and Decorating Workers
occupations.description: Paint, coat, or decorate articles, such as furniture, glass, plateware, pottery, jewelry, toys, books, or leather.

occupations.title: Coating, Painting, and Spraying Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend spraying or rolling machines to coat or paint any of a wide variety of products, including glassware, cloth, ceramics, metal, plastic, paper, or wood, with lacquer, silver, copper, rubber, varnish, glaze, enamel, oil, or rust-proofing materials. Includes painters of transportation vehicles such as painters in auto body repair facilities.

occupations.title: Semiconductor Processing Technicians
occupations.description: Perform any or all of the following functions in the manufacture of electronic semiconductors: load semiconductor material into furnace; saw formed ingots into segments; load individual segment into crystal growing chamber and monitor controls; locate crystal axis in ingot using x-ray equipment and saw ingots into wafers; and clean, polish, and load wafers into series of special purpose furnaces, chemical baths, and equipment used to form circuitry and change conductive properties.

occupations.title: Photographic Process Workers and Processing Machine Operators
occupations.description: Perform work involved in developing and processing photographic images from film or digital media. May perform precision tasks such as editing photographic negatives and prints.

occupations.title: Computer Numerically Controlled Tool Operators
occupations.description: Operate computer-controlled tools, machines, or robots to machine or process parts, tools, or other work pieces made of metal, plastic, wood, stone, or other materials. May also set up and maintain equipment.
titles: Numerical Control Router Set Up Operator
Numerical Control Machine Set Up Operator
Numerical Control Jig Boring Machine Operator
Numerical Control Milling Machine Set Up Operator
CNC Gear Operator (Computer Numerical Control Gear Operator)
CNC Mill Operator (Computer Numerical Control Mill Operator)
CNC Lathe Operator (Computer Numerical Control Lathe Operator)
CNC Laser Operator (Computer Numerical Control Laser Operator)

occupations.title: Computer Numerically Controlled Tool Programmers
occupations.description: Develop programs to control machining or processing of materials by automatic machine tools, equipment, or systems. May also set up, operate, or maintain equipment.
titles: Numerical Control Tool Programmer (NC Tool Programmer)
CNC Mill Programmer (Computer Numerical Control Mill Programmer)
CNC Tool Programmer (Computer Numerical Control Tool Programmer)
CNC Machine Operator (Computer Numerical Control Machine Operator)
CNC Lathe Programmer (Computer Numerical Control Lathe Programmer)
CNC Lathe Operator (Computer Numerically Controlled Lathe Operator)
CNC Machine Programmer (Computer Numerical Control Machine Programmer)
CNC Lathe Programmer (Computer Numerically Controlled Lathe Programmer)
CNC Turning Setup Programmer (Computer Numerical Control Turning Setup Programmer)
CNC Milling Setup Programmer (Computer Numerical Control Milling Setup Programmer)
Sheet Metal CNC Programmer (Sheet Metal Computer Numerically Controlled Programmer)
CNC Process Control Programmer (Computer Numerical Control Process Control Programmer)
CNC Lathe Programmer Operator (Computer Numerically Controlled Lathe Programmer Operator)
CNC Milling and Turning Setup Programmer (Computer Numerical Control Milling and Turning Setup Programmer)

occupations.title: Adhesive Bonding Machine Operators and Tenders
occupations.description: Operate or tend bonding machines that use adhesives to join items for further processing or to form a completed product. Processes include joining veneer sheets into plywood; gluing paper; or joining rubber and rubberized fabric parts, plastic, simulated leather, or other materials.

occupations.title: Cleaning, Washing, and Metal Pickling Equipment Operators and Tenders
occupations.description: Operate or tend machines to wash or clean products, such as barrels or kegs, glass items, tin plate, food, pulp, coal, plastic, or rubber, to remove impurities.

occupations.title: Cooling and Freezing Equipment Operators and Tenders
occupations.description: Operate or tend equipment such as cooling and freezing units, refrigerators, batch freezers, and freezing tunnels, to cool or freeze products, food, blood plasma, and chemicals.

occupations.title: Etchers and Engravers
occupations.description: Engrave or etch metal, wood, rubber, or other materials. Includes such workers as etcher-circuit processors, pantograph engravers, and silk screen etchers.

occupations.title: Molders, Shapers, and Casters, Except Metal and Plastic
occupations.description: Mold, shape, form, cast, or carve products such as food products, figurines, tile, pipes, and candles consisting of clay, glass, plaster, concrete, stone, or combinations of materials.

occupations.title: Stone Cutters and Carvers, Manufacturing
occupations.description: Cut or carve stone according to diagrams and patterns.

occupations.title: Glass Blowers, Molders, Benders, and Finishers
occupations.description: Shape molten glass according to patterns.

occupations.title: Potters, Manufacturing
occupations.description: Operate production machines such as pug mill, jigger machine, or potter's wheel to process clay in manufacture of ceramic, pottery and stoneware products.

occupations.title: Paper Goods Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
occupations.description: Set up, operate, or tend paper goods machines that perform a variety of functions, such as converting, sawing, corrugating, banding, wrapping, boxing, stitching, forming, or sealing paper or paperboard sheets into products.

occupations.title: Tire Builders
occupations.description: Operate machines to build tires.

occupations.title: Helpers--Production Workers
occupations.description: Help production workers by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include supplying or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

occupations.title: Aircraft Cargo Handling Supervisors
occupations.description: Supervise and coordinate the activities of ground crew in the loading, unloading, securing, and staging of aircraft cargo or baggage. May determine the quantity and orientation of cargo and compute aircraft center of gravity. May accompany aircraft as member of flight crew and monitor and handle cargo in flight, and assist and brief passengers on safety and emergency procedures. Includes loadmasters.

occupations.title: First-Line Supervisors of Helpers, Laborers, and Material Movers, Hand
occupations.description: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of helpers, laborers, or material movers, hand.

occupations.title: Recycling Coordinators
occupations.description: Supervise curbside and drop-off recycling programs for municipal governments or private firms.

occupations.title: First-Line Supervisors of Material-Moving Machine and Vehicle Operators
occupations.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of material-moving machine and vehicle operators and helpers.

occupations.title: First-Line Supervisors of Passenger Attendants
occupations.description: Supervise and coordinate activities of passenger attendants.

occupations.title: Airline Pilots, Copilots, and Flight Engineers
occupations.description: Pilot and navigate the flight of fixed-wing aircraft, usually on scheduled air carrier routes, for the transport of passengers and cargo. Requires Federal Air Transport certificate and rating for specific aircraft type used. Includes regional, national, and international airline pilots and flight instructors of airline pilots.

occupations.title: Commercial Pilots
occupations.description: Pilot and navigate the flight of fixed-wing aircraft on nonscheduled air carrier routes, or helicopters. Requires Commercial Pilot certificate. Includes charter pilots with similar certification, and air ambulance and air tour pilots. Excludes regional, national, and international airline pilots.

occupations.title: Air Traffic Controllers
occupations.description: Control air traffic on and within vicinity of airport, and movement of air traffic between altitude sectors and control centers, according to established procedures and policies. Authorize, regulate, and control commercial airline flights according to government or company regulations to expedite and ensure flight safety.
titles: Enroute ATCS (Enroute Air Traffic Control Specialist)
ATC Support Specialist (Air Traffic Control Support Specialist)
Terminal ATC Specialist (Terminal Air Traffic Control Specialist)
Developmental ATCS (Developmental Air Traffic Control Specialist)

occupations.title: Airfield Operations Specialists
occupations.description: Ensure the safe takeoff and landing of commercial and military aircraft. Duties include coordination between air-traffic control and maintenance personnel, dispatching, using airfield landing and navigational aids, implementing airfield safety procedures, monitoring and maintaining flight records, and applying knowledge of weather information.

occupations.title: Flight Attendants
occupations.description: Monitor safety of the aircraft cabin. Provide services to airline passengers, explain safety information, serve food and beverages, and respond to emergency incidents.

occupations.title: Ambulance Drivers and Attendants, Except Emergency Medical Technicians
occupations.description: Drive ambulance or assist ambulance driver in transporting sick, injured, or convalescent persons. Assist in lifting patients.
titles: EMS First Responder (Emergency Medical Services First Responder)
CPR Ambulance Driver (Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation Ambulance Driver)

occupations.title: Driver/Sales Workers
occupations.description: Drive truck or other vehicle over established routes or within an established territory and sell or deliver goods, such as food products, including restaurant take-out items, or pick up or deliver items such as commercial laundry. May also take orders, collect payment, or stock merchandise at point of delivery.

occupations.title: Heavy and Tractor-Trailer Truck Drivers
occupations.description: Drive a tractor-trailer combination or a truck with a capacity of at least 26,001 pounds Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW). May be required to unload truck. Requires commercial drivers' license. Includes tow truck drivers.

occupations.title: Light Truck Drivers
occupations.description: Drive a light vehicle, such as a truck or van, with a capacity of less than 26,001 pounds Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), primarily to pick up merchandise or packages from a distribution center and deliver. May load and unload vehicle.

occupations.title: Bus Drivers, School
occupations.description: Drive a school bus to transport students. Ensure adherence to safety rules. May assist students in boarding or exiting.
titles: SPED Bus Driver (Special Education Bus Driver)
CDL Bus Driver (Commercial Driver's License Bus Driver)
SPED School Bus Driver (Special Education School Bus Driver)
CDL School Bus Driver (Commercial Driver's License School Bus Driver)

occupations.title: Bus Drivers, Transit and Intercity
occupations.description: Drive bus or motor coach, including regular route operations, charters, and private carriage. May assist passengers with baggage. May collect fares or tickets.
titles: CDL Bus Driver (Commercial Driver's License Bus Driver)

occupations.title: Shuttle Drivers and Chauffeurs
occupations.description: Drive a motor vehicle to transport passengers on a planned or scheduled basis. May collect a fare. Includes nonemergency medical transporters and hearse drivers.

occupations.title: Locomotive Engineers
occupations.description: Drive electric, diesel-electric, steam, or gas-turbine-electric locomotives to transport passengers or freight. Interpret train orders, electronic or manual signals, and railroad rules and regulations.

occupations.title: Rail Yard Engineers, Dinkey Operators, and Hostlers
occupations.description: Drive switching or other locomotive or dinkey engines within railroad yard, industrial plant, quarry, construction project, or similar location.

occupations.title: Railroad Brake, Signal, and Switch Operators and Locomotive Firers
occupations.description: Operate or monitor railroad track switches or locomotive instruments. May couple or uncouple rolling stock to make up or break up trains. Watch for and relay traffic signals. May inspect couplings, air hoses, journal boxes, and hand brakes. May watch for dragging equipment or obstacles on rights-of-way.

occupations.title: Railroad Conductors and Yardmasters
occupations.description: Coordinate activities of switch-engine crew within railroad yard, industrial plant, or similar location. Conductors coordinate activities of train crew on passenger or freight trains. Yardmasters review train schedules and switching orders and coordinate activities of workers engaged in railroad traffic operations, such as the makeup or breakup of trains and yard switching.

occupations.title: Subway and Streetcar Operators
occupations.description: Operate subway or elevated suburban trains with no separate locomotive, or electric-powered streetcar, to transport passengers. May handle fares.

occupations.title: Sailors and Marine Oilers
occupations.description: Stand watch to look for obstructions in path of vessel, measure water depth, turn wheel on bridge, or use emergency equipment as directed by captain, mate, or pilot. Break out, rig, overhaul, and store cargo-handling gear, stationary rigging, and running gear. Perform a variety of maintenance tasks to preserve the painted surface of the ship and to maintain line and ship equipment. Must hold government-issued certification and tankerman certification when working aboard liquid-carrying vessels. Includes able seamen and ordinary seamen.

occupations.title: Captains, Mates, and Pilots of Water Vessels
occupations.description: Command or supervise operations of ships and water vessels, such as tugboats and ferryboats. Required to hold license issued by U.S. Coast Guard.

occupations.title: Motorboat Operators
occupations.description: Operate small motor-driven boats. May assist in navigational activities.

occupations.title: Ship Engineers
occupations.description: Supervise and coordinate activities of crew engaged in operating and maintaining engines, boilers, deck machinery, and electrical, sanitary, and refrigeration equipment aboard ship.
titles: Officer in Charge of Engineering Watch (OICEW)

occupations.title: Bridge and Lock Tenders
occupations.description: Operate and tend bridges, canal locks, and lighthouses to permit marine passage on inland waterways, near shores, and at danger points in waterway passages. May supervise such operations. Includes drawbridge operators, lock operators, and slip bridge operators.

occupations.title: Parking Attendants
occupations.description: Park vehicles or issue tickets for customers in a parking lot or garage. May park or tend vehicles in environments such as a car dealership or rental car facility. May collect fee.

occupations.title: Automotive and Watercraft Service Attendants
occupations.description: Service automobiles, buses, trucks, boats, and other automotive or marine vehicles with fuel, lubricants, and accessories. Collect payment for services and supplies. May lubricate vehicle, change motor oil, refill antifreeze, or replace lights or other accessories, such as windshield wiper blades or fan belts. May repair or replace tires.

occupations.title: Aircraft Service Attendants
occupations.description: Service aircraft with fuel. May de-ice aircraft, refill water and cooling agents, empty sewage tanks, service air and oxygen systems, or clean and polish exterior.

occupations.title: Traffic Technicians
occupations.description: Conduct field studies to determine traffic volume, speed, effectiveness of signals, adequacy of lighting, and other factors influencing traffic conditions, under direction of traffic engineer.
titles: Highway Traffic Control Technician (Highway Traffic Control Tech)

occupations.title: Transportation Inspectors
occupations.description: Inspect equipment or goods in connection with the safe transport of cargo or people. Includes rail transportation inspectors, such as freight inspectors, rail inspectors, and other inspectors of transportation vehicles not elsewhere classified.

occupations.title: Aviation Inspectors
occupations.description: Inspect aircraft, maintenance procedures, air navigational aids, air traffic controls, and communications equipment to ensure conformance with Federal safety regulations.
titles: Aircraft Quality Control Inspector (Aircraft QC Inspector)

occupations.title: Transportation Vehicle, Equipment and Systems Inspectors, Except Aviation
occupations.description: Inspect and monitor transportation equipment, vehicles, or systems to ensure compliance with regulations and safety standards.

occupations.title: Passenger Attendants
occupations.description: Provide services to ensure the safety of passengers aboard ships, buses, trains, or within the station or terminal. Perform duties such as explaining the use of safety equipment, serving meals or beverages, or answering questions related to travel.

occupations.title: Conveyor Operators and Tenders
occupations.description: Control or tend conveyors or conveyor systems that move materials or products to and from stockpiles, processing stations, departments, or vehicles. May control speed and routing of materials or products.

occupations.title: Crane and Tower Operators
occupations.description: Operate mechanical boom and cable or tower and cable equipment to lift and move materials, machines, or products in many directions.

occupations.title: Dredge Operators
occupations.description: Operate dredge to remove sand, gravel, or other materials in order to excavate and maintain navigable channels in waterways.

occupations.title: Hoist and Winch Operators
occupations.description: Operate or tend hoists or winches to lift and pull loads using power-operated cable equipment.

occupations.title: Industrial Truck and Tractor Operators
occupations.description: Operate industrial trucks or tractors equipped to move materials around a warehouse, storage yard, factory, construction site, or similar location.

occupations.title: Cleaners of Vehicles and Equipment
occupations.description: Wash or otherwise clean vehicles, machinery, and other equipment. Use such materials as water, cleaning agents, brushes, cloths, and hoses.

occupations.title: Laborers and Freight, Stock, and Material Movers, Hand
occupations.description: Manually move freight, stock, luggage, or other materials, or perform other general labor. Includes all manual laborers not elsewhere classified.

occupations.title: Recycling and Reclamation Workers
occupations.description: Prepare and sort materials or products for recycling. Identify and remove hazardous substances. Dismantle components of products such as appliances.
titles: Convenience Recycle Center Technician (Convenience Recycle Center Tech)
Deconstruction and Decontamination Waste Operations Specialist (D and D Waste Operations Specialist)

occupations.title: Machine Feeders and Offbearers
occupations.description: Feed materials into or remove materials from machines or equipment that is automatic or tended by other workers.

occupations.title: Packers and Packagers, Hand
occupations.description: Pack or package by hand a wide variety of products and materials.

occupations.title: Stockers and Order Fillers
occupations.description: Receive, store, and issue merchandise, materials, equipment, and other items from stockroom, warehouse, or storage yard to fill shelves, racks, tables, or customers' orders. May operate power equipment to fill orders. May mark prices on merchandise and set up sales displays.

occupations.title: Gas Compressor and Gas Pumping Station Operators
occupations.description: Operate steam-, gas-, electric motor-, or internal combustion-engine driven compressors. Transmit, compress, or recover gases, such as butane, nitrogen, hydrogen, and natural gas.
titles: Liquefied Natural Gas Plant Operator (LNG Plant Operator)

occupations.title: Pump Operators, Except Wellhead Pumpers
occupations.description: Tend, control, or operate power-driven, stationary, or portable pumps and manifold systems to transfer gases, oil, other liquids, slurries, or powdered materials to and from various vessels and processes.

occupations.title: Wellhead Pumpers
occupations.description: Operate power pumps and auxiliary equipment to produce flow of oil or gas from wells in oil field.

occupations.title: Refuse and Recyclable Material Collectors
occupations.description: Collect and dump refuse or recyclable materials from containers into truck. May drive truck.

occupations.title: Tank Car, Truck, and Ship Loaders
occupations.description: Load and unload chemicals and bulk solids, such as coal, sand, and grain, into or from tank cars, trucks, or ships, using material moving equipment. May perform a variety of other tasks relating to shipment of products. May gauge or sample shipping tanks and test them for leaks.
